newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard unloads big drug haul.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard unloads big drug haul.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard on Thursday unloaded a major haul of cocaine tossed overboard by Caribbean drug runners as they fled from authorities along the Central America coast.
A Coast Guard crew carried bale after bale from the cutter Spencer at a Coast Guard station in Miami Beach, Florida, more than three weeks after the seizure was made off the coast of Honduras.
"Nearly 4,000 pounds, that's a big haul," Coast Guard Petty Officer Charles Smith said.
Coast Guard officials said a helicopter crew spotted a 40-foot (12-metre) speedboat carrying bales of cocaine on April 22 about 16 miles (26 km) northeast of Honduras.
The helicopter chased the boat as the three crew began dumping bales overboard. The Spencer could not catch the boat, which fled to the Honduran coast, officials said.
The cutter's crew picked up 71 bales of cocaine, wrapped in nine layers of burlap and plastic, totalling 3,905 pounds (1,775 kg), officials said. It was turned over to the U.S. Customs Service.
